name: creating
description: A sense that you are in the process of changing something into something else, generally with the intention of creating some kind of order in the environment.
perceptions: The world could use more of something.
I can help make that happen.
I have the materials, tools, and time needed.
results: If creating something is for fun, it can be a joy.
If it's your job and you've created the same thing many times, it may not be fun.
examples: A kid drawing a picture for grandma.

guidance.description: There are many sites that give ideas on how to cultivate creativity. Here are a few.

comparisons.description: Generally 'creating' is about increasing order in the world, or at least preserving order while changing its form. 'Destroying' is about decreasing order - breaking something into smaller parts. 'Fixing' is about restoring something to it's desired form or functionality after having been degraded in some way.

commentaries.quote: To be creative means to be in love with life. You can be creative only if you love life enough that you want to enhance its beauty, you want to bring a little more music to it, a little more poetry to it, a little more dance to it.
A rock pile ceases to be a rock pile the moment a single man contemplates it, bearing within him the image of a cathedral.
The whole difference between construction and creation is exactly this: that a thing constructed can only be loved after it is constructed; but a thing created is loved before it exists.
Another flaw in the human character is that everybody wants to build and nobody wants to do maintenance.
Consciousness expresses itself through creation. This world we live in is the dance of the creator.
The biggest emotion in creation is the bridge to optimism.
We don't make things out of nothing. We assemble them out of graphite, paint, blank paper, keyboards, time, inspiration, and other scraps.
Sometimes you have to destroy something to create something else. We pull weeds to have a garden, cut trees to have a house, and let go of one relationship for another.
It's worth pointing out that creating isn't always good, and destroying isn't always bad. After all, we can create indiscriminately powerful weapons and we can destroy a wasp nest on the front door.
